Answer: C
Reason: The ultrasound images show a cystic lesion in the fetal thorax. In cases of congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) or bronchogenic cysts located in the lower lobe, they are typically adjacent to the heart and diaphragm. Unless very large causing mediastinal shift (which would be described as compression/displacement), smaller lesions like those often seen antenatally might just be adjacent without significant mass effect on the heart position or diaphragm elevation/depression initially, or the description fits a localized lower lobe finding. Option C describes a location (lower lobe) and relationship (adjacent to heart, intact diaphragm, no mediastinal shift) that is consistent with a non-compressive or mildly compressive lesion often found in this region, distinguishing it from upper/middle lobe locations or massive lesions causing severe shift. Looking closely at the provided crops, the lesion is central/inferior relative to the spine, consistent with a lower lobe origin near the mediastinum/diaphragm.
